_comment: TX engine API allowlist, kept by hand (no generator). tools/api_audit.py reads it; check_lua.py reads 'globals' and 'base_includes'.
Sections: globals (engine global names), static ('Root.Member' / 'Root:Method', wildcards allowed), methods (':Name' without receiver),
events ('Events.X', 'GameEvents.X', 'LuaEvents.X', wildcards allowed), gameinfo (GameInfo table names), base_includes (base-game include
name -> globals it defines), forbidden ([{name, why}] extra forbidden identifiers).
A context missing from 'ctx' means the call may not be used there (ERROR). 'only_paths' limits a call to files whose path contains one of the strings.
Status ('level'): C = verified in game. L (likely), NV (new, verify), PENDING and VERIFY are not verified: every use is a WARN and is listed in the checklist.
Add an entry only with evidence in refs/note: a base-game file:line, a shipped mod, or a spike result (S1..S4, V1..V12).
Seeded 2026-10-03 from the Expeditionary mod (EFV 1.0.x, source 'EFV'): only calls EFV's own code used (EFV or EFV_Dev), only the contexts where EFV had them at level C,
evidence fields kept as EFV wrote them (refs like A47 / U16 / T09 / Session C point into EFV's PLAN and test sessions). GameEvents.EFV_* / LuaEvents.EFV_* became
GameEvents.TX_* / LuaEvents.TX_*. Calls EFV only allowed in EFV_Dev are limited to TX_Dev/ here. base_includes is copied unchanged (harvested from base-game UI files).
Spike probes (TX_Probe / Probe calls) are not audited and need no entry; see tools/README.md.
A context may carry its own "only_paths", "source", "refs" and "note": then it is limited on its own. TX_Dev contexts added to EFV entries use this (e.g. PlayerConfigurations G: NV, TX_Dev/ only).
